title: Canonical transport between equal representatives of a filtered category colimit
statement:
Let $J$ be a small filtered category, $D:J\to\mathsf{Cat}$ a strict functor with small values, and $C$ its object-and-arrow set colimit with structure functors $v_i:D(i)\to C$ [def-nagata-category], [def-weil-size-convention], [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-categories]. Let $\mathcal A$ be a category in the containing universe. Suppose given functors $A_i:D(i)\to\mathcal A$ and natural isomorphisms $\theta_a:A_kD(a)\to A_i$ for $a:i\to k$, with $\theta_1=1$ and $\theta_{ba}=\theta_a\circ(\theta_bD(a))$. A representative is a pair $p=(i,x)$ with $x\in D(i)$, and $|p|=v_i(x)$. If $p=(i,x)$ and $q=(j,y)$ have $|p|=|q|$, choose $a:i\to k$, $b:j\to k$ with $D(a)x=D(b)y$. The isomorphism
$$T^A_{pq}:=\theta_{b,y}\circ\theta_{a,x}^{-1}:A_i(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_j(y)$$
(where the middle objects are identified by the displayed equality) is independent of $k,a,b$ and the equality witness. For any three representatives of the same object, $T^A_{pp}=1$ and $T^A_{qr}T^A_{pq}=T^A_{pr}$. If $q=(k,D(a)x)$, then $T^A_{pq}=\theta_{a,x}^{-1}$.

If $f:x\to y$ in $D(i)$ and $g:x'\to y'$ in $D(j)$ have equal images as complete arrows in $C$, then
$$T^A_{(i,y),(j,y')}\circ A_i(f)=A_j(g)\circ T^A_{(i,x),(j,x')}.$$
For any second family $(B_i,\eta_a)$ satisfying the same coherence conditions and natural transformations $\rho_i:A_i\to B_i$ with $\rho_i\theta_a=\eta_a(\rho_kD(a))$, transport satisfies
$$\rho_j(y)\circ T^A_{pq}=T^B_{pq}\circ\rho_i(x).$$
Postcomposition by any functor $H:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ sends $T^A_{pq}$ to $T^{HA}_{pq}$.

source.place: Tag 04AX (section-directed-colimits), eventual equality of representatives. The conjugation and modification identities below are an agent formulation extending that representative calculus; they are not asserted verbatim by this tag.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] to the object-set diagram $D\mathbin{\circ}\mathsf{Cat.objects}$ (Mathlib Types.FilteredColimit.colimit_eq_iff). It gives a common-stage witness $a:i\to k,b:j\to k$ for equal representatives $x,y$. The actual definition evaluates $\theta_{a,x}^{-1}$, the equality isomorphism of the two middle objects, and $\theta_{b,y}$ at a witness chosen from this proved equality criterion.

source.place: Tag 04AX (section-directed-colimits), eventual equality of set representatives; Tag 002V (definition-directed), common targets and equalization of parallel arrows. The coherence calculations are an agent argument, not a theorem asserted by these tags.

proof.text:
First check invariance under one further transition $c:k\to l$. The coherence hypotheses give $\theta_{ca,x}=\theta_{a,x}\theta_{c,D(a)x}$ and $\theta_{cb,y}=\theta_{b,y}\theta_{c,D(b)y}$. Since both middle objects equal $z$, direct cancellation gives
$$T(ca,cb)=\theta_{b,y}\theta_{c,z}(\theta_{a,x}\theta_{c,z})^{-1}=\theta_{b,y}\theta_{a,x}^{-1}=T(a,b).$$
These expressions use the identifications induced by the displayed object equalities; applying a functor to an object equality and composing those identifications respects reflexivity and transitivity.

source.place: Tag 04AX (section-directed-colimits), eventual equality of set representatives; Tag 002V (definition-directed), common targets and equalization of parallel arrows. The coherence calculations are an agent argument, not a theorem asserted by these tags.

proof.text:
Compare witnesses $(k,a,b)$ and $(l,a',b')$ for the same $p,q$. By the filteredness axioms in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], choose $c:k\to m$ and $d:l\to m$. Equalize the parallel arrows $ca,da':i\to m$ by postcomposing with one arrow; next equalize the resulting parallel arrows from $j$ obtained from $cb,db'$. The second postcomposition preserves the first equality. Thus, renaming the composites $c,d$, we have $ca=da'$ and $cb=db'$. Step 2 gives
$$T(a,b)=T(ca,cb)=T(da',db')=T(a',b').$$
Strictness of $D$ identifies the common middle objects in this calculation. Equality of objects is a proposition, so two proofs of that equality give the same identification (in Lean, proof irrelevance). This proves all the required choice independence and defines $T^A_{pq}$. In Lean, IsFiltered.bowtie packages the common-target and two-equalizer construction; witness_refine then compares both formulas at that common refinement.

source.place: Tag 04AX (section-directed-colimits), eventual equality of set representatives; Tag 002V (definition-directed), common targets and equalization of parallel arrows. The coherence calculations are an agent argument, not a theorem asserted by these tags.

proof.text: For $p=q$, compute with $k=i$ and $a=b=1_i$ to obtain $T^A_{pp}=1$. If $q=(k,D(a)x)$, use the witness consisting of $a:i\to k$ and $1_k:k\to k$. The normalization $\theta_1=1$ gives $T^A_{pq}=\theta_{a,x}^{-1}$. Independence proved in Step 3 makes these computations valid for the canonical transports.

source.place: Tag 04AX (section-directed-colimits), eventual equality of set representatives; Tag 002V (definition-directed), common targets and equalization of parallel arrows. The coherence calculations are an agent argument, not a theorem asserted by these tags.

proof.text:
For $p=(i,x),q=(j,y),r=(h,z)$ representing the same object, take witnesses $(a:i\to k,b:j\to k)$ for $p,q$ and $(c:j\to l,d:h\to l)$ for $q,r$, as in Step 1. Choose $u:k\to m,v:l\to m$ and then equalize $ub,vc:j\to m$, using [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. After this postcomposition there are maps $\alpha:i\to n$, $\beta:j\to n$, $\gamma:h\to n$ with $D(\alpha)x=D(\beta)y=D(\gamma)z$. By Step 3 all three transports can be computed using these witnesses. Hence
$$T^A_{qr}T^A_{pq}=(\theta_{\gamma,z}\theta_{\beta,y}^{-1})(\theta_{\beta,y}\theta_{\alpha,x}^{-1})=\theta_{\gamma,z}\theta_{\alpha,x}^{-1}=T^A_{pr}.$$
The common-target choice and one equalization are precisely the two filteredness axioms, rather than an assumption that $J$ is a poset. In Lean, IsFiltered.span packages the common-target and middle-arrow equalization, and witness_comp cancels the common middle comparison and composes the equality isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 04AX (section-directed-colimits), eventual equality of set representatives; Tag 002V (definition-directed), common targets and equalization of parallel arrows. The coherence calculations are an agent argument, not a theorem asserted by these tags.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] directly to $D\mathbin{\circ}\mathsf{Cat.arrows}$. The resulting equality is an equality of complete stage arrows. Arrow.mk_eq_mk_iff extracts endpoint equalities $e_x,e_y$ and the equation $D(a)f=\mathrm{eqToHom}(e_x)D(b)g\mathrm{eqToHom}(e_y^{-1})$. Applying $F_k$ gives a commuting square. Naturality of $\theta_a^{-1}$ and $\theta_b$ composes this square into the desired transport square. Independence computes both endpoint transports at the same witness. No category structure on the colimit is needed.

source.place: Tag 04AX (section-directed-colimits), eventual equality of set representatives; Tag 002V (definition-directed), common targets and equalization of parallel arrows. The coherence calculations are an agent argument, not a theorem asserted by these tags.

proof.text:
For a compatible family $\rho$ and any witness $a:i\to k,b:j\to k$ with middle object $z$, its two compatibility equations read $\rho_i(x)\theta^A_{a,x}=\eta_{a,x}\rho_k(z)$ and $\rho_j(y)\theta^A_{b,y}=\eta_{b,y}\rho_k(z)$. Since $\eta_{a,x}$ and $\theta^A_{a,x}$ are invertible, the first gives $\rho_k(z)(\theta^A_{a,x})^{-1}=\eta_{a,x}^{-1}\rho_i(x)$. Substituting into the second gives
$$\rho_j(y)T^A_{pq}=\eta_{b,y}\rho_k(z)(\theta^A_{a,x})^{-1}=\eta_{b,y}\eta_{a,x}^{-1}\rho_i(x)=T^B_{pq}\rho_i(x).$$
This does not invert $\rho_i$ or $\rho_k$; the transformations $\rho_i$ need not be isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 04AX (section-directed-colimits), eventual equality of set representatives; Tag 002V (definition-directed), common targets and equalization of parallel arrows. The coherence calculations are an agent argument, not a theorem asserted by these tags.

proof.text:
For any functor $H:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, postcomposition has comparisons $H\theta_a$ satisfying the same coherence by preservation of composition and identities. Compute its transport with the same $a,b$ used for $T^A_{pq}$. A functor sends an inverse isomorphism to the inverse of its image, since applying it to the two inverse equations gives the two inverse equations in $\mathcal B$. Therefore
$$H(T^A_{pq})=H(\theta_{b,y})H(\theta_{a,x})^{-1}=T^{HA}_{pq}.$$
The equality identifications of the middle objects are also preserved by $H$, as is checked by substituting the object equality with reflexivity. Step 3 removes the choice of witness in this calculation.
